newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 14.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 14.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Monday and main factors likely to affect trading:

* The market is seen persisting in a consolidation mood for the week and Monday's trade will likely be dampened by the Dow's fall last Friday as well as concerns over the recent announcement of oil price increases, Elline Salvatierra, analyst at Dharmala Securities Phils Inc said.
* Anscor-Hagedorn Securities says with an uptrend in local and U.S. interest rates, any rally may be limited.

* Asian Capital Equities Inc says in its weekly market outlook that some technical rallies may be seen despite a generally weak market as investors may accumulate stocks while awaiting the release of first quarter earnings results.
* Anscor adds in its weekly technical forecast that the market may test a bottom of 2,850- points before staging any stronger rallies.
* On Friday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index rose 27.76 points to 2,976.78.
* Petron Corp and Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp announced on Friday an oil price increase by an average of 1.46 centavos per litre on wholesale posted prices.

* Newspaper BusinessWorld, quoting a ranking Department of Finance official, says the finance department is confident the public sector will have a four billion peso surplus this year with the improved performance of government-owned and-controlled corporations.

* Today reports that based on Central Bank data, there was an acceleration in outward investments in 1996 that pushed down net foreign investments by 24.4 percent to $1.06 billion last year from $1.61 billion in 1995.

* Times Journal says the Securities and Exchange Commission is planning to revoke the license of brokers circulating rumours to manipulate prices of securities listed at the Philippine Stock Exchange.
* The Central Bank says bank lending rates have dropped to an average of 13.1 percent as of March this year compared to the average 15.1 percent a year ago.

* San Miguel Corp said the deal between its Coca-Cola subsidiary and Coca-Cola Amatil was fair and made sense. Under the deal, San Miguel will sell 70 percent owned subsidiary Coca Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc in exchange for a 25 percent stake in Coca-Cola Amatil.
* On Friday, the Dow Jones dropped 148.36 points to 6,391.69. PLDT's ADR rose $0 3/4 to $59.
* The peso closed higher at 26.363 to the dollar vs 26.365.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was unchanged at 10.03125 percent.
